pick.name: Auto mode + allow/deny rules, plus the Bash sandbox (macOS, Linux, WSL2)
pick.what: Classifier-gated autonomy with explicit rules; OS-level sandbox for Bash
pick.why: First-party; sandbox gives filesystem/network isolation that rules alone cannot
pick.free_limits: Requires a Claude plan or API billing

alts.name: Bypass permissions (current)
alts.why: Fastest but unsandboxed; reserve for throwaway environments
alts.free_limits: Requires a Claude plan (Pro/Max plans/Team/Enterprise) or API billing; counts against plan usage

alts.name: Anthropic sandbox-runtime
alts.what: Optional npm package adding seccomp Unix-socket blocking and standalone sandboxing

candidates.name: Dev containers
candidates.verdict: regulated or client code, any OS

decision: Use auto mode with explicit deny rules instead of bypass permissions. For unknown repos turn on the Bash sandbox (/sandbox) where available, or use a dev container.
details: Generalised: sandbox covers macOS and Linux natively, Windows only inside WSL2. Auto mode and the sandbox need Claude Code (a paid plan or API billing); dev containers are the free isolation option.

os_notes.macOS: Bash sandbox uses built-in Seatbelt; nothing to install; run /sandbox.
os_notes.Windows: Native Windows is not sandboxed (commands run unsandboxed). Run Claude Code inside WSL2 (not WSL1) to get /sandbox; use deny rules or a dev container natively.
os_notes.Linux: Sandbox needs bubblewrap and socat (sudo apt-get install bubblewrap socat); on Ubuntu 24.04+ AppArmor may block user namespaces and need a bwrap profile.

verify.note: Verified: sandbox runs on macOS (Seatbelt), Linux and WSL2 (bubblewrap + socat); WSL1 unsupported; native Windows runs commands unsandboxed. os_notes accurate.
